query: electronic hand hygiene monitoring real-time feedback cluster randomised trial wards compliance outcome
sourcesConsulted: model knowledge of the hand hygiene literature
gradeRationale: Certainty is left to the appraisal of the retrieved records.
synthesis: Four further leads are suggested alongside the retrieved records: a landmark multicentre study linking compliance to infection, a study of gaming of electronic monitoring, a report on blinded video review as an outcome, and a synthesis of staff views on surveillance. None has been retrieved or checked.

items.title: Hand hygiene compliance and hospital-onset infection across 40 hospitals: the landmark multicentre evidence
items.keyFindings: Hospitals with higher observed compliance had lower hospital-onset infection rates.
items.notes: Presented as a landmark study; not retrieved.

items.title: Gaming of electronic hand hygiene monitoring: dispenser activation without patient contact
items.keyFindings: Video review found that a fifth of dispenser activations logged at patient-zone entry were not followed by hand rubbing.
items.limitations: Two wards; video only in corridors.

items.title: Observer-blinded video review as an outcome in hand hygiene trials
items.keyFindings: Video review by assessors unaware of allocation agreed well with live observation and removed observer visibility.
items.limitations: Privacy approval was difficult and cameras covered only doorways.

items.title: Staff perceptions of surveillance in electronic hand hygiene monitoring: a synthesis
items.keyFindings: Acceptance depended on written limits on individual data use.
items.limitations: Mostly nursing staff in high-income settings.

summary: Four unchecked leads suggested; one is presented as a landmark and one carries a year that is not a number.
